Hyundai Reveals All 2027 Model Year Changes to American Lineup, Confirms All-New Tucson ICE & HEV
6 photos
Photo: Hyundai
The South Korean automaker has made it easier for all of us to track the modifications to the 2027MY lineup by compiling a list of changes for them – and we have two major confirmations along with a specialty model.
First, Hyundai has reconfirmed that the all-new NX5 fifth-generation Tucson is coming to America for the 2027 model year, packing the fresh “Art of Steel” design, more passenger and cargo space, both ICE and hybrid powertrains, and the next-generation Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Mechanically, the 2027 Tucson will use Hyundai’s 1.6-liter turbocharged GDI four-cylinder, producing 184 hp and 195 lb.-ft. of torque paired to an eight-speed automatic transmission. The 1.6L turbo hybrid system has a combined output of 233 hp and 280 lb-ft of torque, paired with a six-speed auto. Both are available with FWD or HTRAC all-wheel drive, and towing capacity is up to 2,500 lbs. on ICE models and 3,000 lbs. on the HEV.
The company, most importantly, said that the XRT PRO model is a hybrid-only, adventure-focused version with HTRAC AWD, a suspension lift, 8.3 inches of ground clearance, and 18-inch wheels plus all-terrain tires. It will include the X-Trek+ off-road technology “with real-time terrain assessment and Target Speed Control.”
The specialty novelty is the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 6 N, which is arriving during the spring season of 2027 with 601-hp dual-motor AWD, and up to 641 hp and 568 lb.-ft. of torque using N Grin Boost. The EV will sprint to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds with N Launch Control and has a 159-mph top speed. The 84.0-kWh battery is good for up to 245 miles of all-electric range, and thanks to the 800V platform, it can recharge 10–80% in approximately 18 minutes with a compatible 350-kW DC fast charger.
It also gets a standard NACS charging port and a CCS adapter, along with N Performance technology: the N e-Shift with simulated performance gear changes, N Active Sound+ with selectable performance sound profiles, N Launch Control, N Pedal, N Drift Optimizer, and more. The third major novelty for 2027 is the 2027 Hyundai Elantra – the eighth generation of the compact car series was launched in June 2026 as the Avante at the Busan International Mobility Show in Busan, South Korea, but the company is still keeping the Elantra details under wraps – most likely for a surprise premiere at the upcoming LA Auto Show (November 20-29).
The rest of the lineup is comprised of the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 and 5 N (EV), Hyundai IONIQ 9 (EV), Hyundai Palisade (ICE, HEV), Hyundai Santa Fe (ICE, HEV), Hyundai Santa Cruz (ICE), Hyundai Kona (ICE), Hyundai Venue (ICE), which are carryover models with minor changes, and the Hyundai Sonata (ICE, HEV, N Line), which features no changes at all.
